results.answer:
As a federal retiree with an OPM annuity who isn't entitled to Social Security or RRB benefits, you must ask to have your Part B premiums deducted from your annuity. Contact your local Social Security office to make your request. Visit SSA.gov/locator to find your local office.

If you don't set up the deduction, you'll get a bill for your Part B premium. Typically, Part B premiums are billed quarterly (every 3 months). If you also pay for Part A or Part D IRMAA, or use Medicare Easy Pay to pay your premiums, you'll get a monthly bill. There are 4 ways to pay your premium bill. The excerpts describe two of them:
- Online through your secure Medicare account: Visit Medicare.gov/account to log into (or create) your Medicare account. Then, select "Pay my premium" to make a payment by credit card, debit card, Health Savings Account (HSA) card, or from your checking or savings account. This free service is the fastest way to pay your premium.
- Medicare Easy Pay: This free service automatically deducts your payment from an account. The rest of this description is cut off in the excerpt.

results.answer:
Under Basic Option, Self Only, there is no deductible to meet first. Basic Option does not have a calendar year deductible. Instead, most services are subject to copayments ($35 for primary care providers and $50 for specialists).

If you stay with PPO (Preferred) providers, the most you would pay in a year is **$7,500**. For a Self Only enrollment, your out-of-pocket maximum for eligible coinsurance and copayment amounts is $7,500 when you use Preferred providers. Once you reach it, you no longer have to pay the associated cost-sharing amounts for the rest of the calendar year.

Some caveats:
- Only eligible expenses for Preferred provider services count toward these limits.
- Some costs do not count toward this protection.
- Under Basic Option, you must use Preferred providers in order to receive benefits, except in cases of medical emergency or accidental injury.

For comparison, Standard Option does have a calendar year deductible is $350 per person, and its Self Only PPO maximum is $6,000.

results.answer:
On Basic Option, an MRI done and billed by a facility falls under outpatient diagnostic testing and treatment services performed and billed by a facility, limited to: ... CT scans/MRIs/PET scans. What you pay depends on the facility type:

- Preferred facilities: **$250** copayment per day per facility
- Member facilities: **$250** copayment per day per facility
- Non-member facilities: **$250** copayment per day per facility, plus any difference between our allowance and the billed amount

You may owe more in two situations:
- You pay 35% of the Plan allowance for agents or drugs administered or obtained in connection with your care. This could include contrast used for the MRI.
- You may be responsible for paying a higher copayment per day per facility if other diagnostic and/or treatment services are billed in addition to the services listed here.

results.answer:
Under Original Medicare, day 45 falls in the second tier of a skilled nursing facility benefit period: Days 21–100: You pay $217 each day.

For context, the full schedule within a benefit period is:
- Days 1–20: You pay $0 each day after you pay the $1,736 amount.
- Days 21–100: You pay $217 each day.
- Days 101 and beyond: You pay all costs.

Also note that your benefit period ends when you stop getting skilled nursing facility care for 60 days in a row. If your mom is in a Medicare Advantage Plan instead, those plans can't charge more than Original Medicare for certain services, like chemotherapy, dialysis, and days 21–100 of skilled nursing facility care.

results.answer:
On Basic Option, for an inpatient hospital stay at **Preferred facilities** you pay $425 per day copayment up to $2,975 per admission. So the cap is **$2,975 per admission**.

A few related points:
- **Maternity:** For Preferred facility care related to maternity, including care at Preferred birthing facilities, your responsibility for covered inpatient services is limited to $425 per admission. This copayment is waived if you deliver in a Blue Distinction facility. The excerpt cuts off at that point.
- **With Medicare:** The Section 9 summary shows Basic Option inpatient hospital cost as $425/day up to $2,975 without Medicare, and Basic Option With Medicare Parts A & B: $0.00.
- **Extended stays:** If you need to stay longer in the hospital than initially planned, we will cover an extended stay if it is medically necessary. However, you must precertify the extended stay.

For comparison, Standard Option charges a $350 per admission copayment for unlimited days (no deductible) at Preferred facilities.

results.answer:
Completing the Blue Health Assessment (BHA) gets you the following:

- **A health action plan:** The BHA questionnaire is an easy and engaging online health evaluation program which can be completed in 10-20 minutes. Your BHA answers are evaluated to create a unique health action plan.
- **Health account dollars:** After completing the BHA, you may access Daily Habits to set personalized goals. We will add $40 to your health account for each goal achieved, up to a maximum of three goals per year. By completing the BHA and a maximum of three health goals, you can earn up to a total of $170 in health account dollars. These excerpts don't state the BHA's own reward separately. You must complete the BHA and your selected goals during the calendar year in order to receive these incentives.
- **A possible free blood pressure monitor:** If you complete the Blue Health Assessment (BHA), and indicate that you have been diagnosed with hypertension, and at least one medical claim has been processed during the past 12 months with a reported diagnosis of hypertension, you become eligible. You are eligible to receive a free BPM every two calendar years.

These features apply to both Standard and Basic Option.

results.answer:
A doctor who doesn't accept assignment can charge **15%** above the Medicare-approved amount. In many cases, the charge can't be more than 15% above the Medicare-approved amount for non-participating healthcare providers. This amount is called "the limiting charge." The BCBS brochure gives the same limit as a total: such a physician may not bill you for more than 115% of the amount Medicare bases its payment on, called the "limiting charge."

Opt-out physicians are different. Should you visit an opt-out physician, the physician will not be limited to 115% of the Medicare-approved amount.

If you have the BCBS Service Benefit Plan and your physician doesn't accept assignment, you pay the difference between the "limiting charge" or the physician's charge (whichever is less) and our payment combined with Medicare's payment. Under Basic Option, you must see Preferred providers in order to receive benefits.

If a doctor charges more than the limit, ask the physician to reduce the charges. If the physician does not, report the physician to the Medicare carrier that sent you the MSN form.

results.answer:
With Original Medicare, you appeal using your Medicare Summary Notice (MSN). The steps are:

- Get the "Medicare Summary Notice" (MSN) that shows the item or service you're appealing.
- Circle the item(s) on the MSN you disagree with. Write an explanation of why you disagree with the decision. You can write on the MSN or on a separate piece of paper and attach it to the MSN.
- Include your name, phone number, and Medicare Number on the MSN. Keep a copy for your records.
- Send the MSN, or a copy, to the company that handles bills for Medicare (Medicare Administrative Contractor) listed on the MSN. You can include any information you have about your appeal, like information from your health care provider.

Instead of the MSN, you can use Form CMS-20027. To get this form, visit Medicare.gov/basics/forms-publications-mailings/forms/appeals, or call 1-800-MEDICARE (1-800-633-4227) to have a copy mailed to you.

Deadlines and timing:
- You must file your appeal by the date in the MSN. If you missed the deadline for appealing, you may still file an appeal and get a decision if you can show good cause for missing the deadline.
- You'll generally get a decision from the Medicare Administrative Contractor within **60 days** after they get your request. If Medicare will cover the item(s) or service(s), it will be listed on your next MSN.

You can also ask your doctor, supplier, or other health care provider for any information to make your appeal stronger. You can also get help filing an appeal from your State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP).

results.answer:
Generally, no. Under Basic Option you must use Preferred providers in order to receive benefits. There are no benefits for care performed by Participating and Non-participating providers. For example, for diabetic education under Basic Option, the Participating/Non-participating cost is listed as You pay all charges.

There are some exceptions:

- **Emergencies and certain other circumstances:** You must use Preferred providers for your care to be eligible for benefits, except in certain circumstances, such as emergency care. See Section 3 for exceptions under What you must do to get covered care.
- **Overseas care:** The Basic Option requirement to use Preferred providers in order to receive benefits does not apply when you receive overseas care.
